Bayesian proxy-SVAR on top of bvarm() draws

Source: R/psvar-bayes.R
varm_proxy_bayes.Rd

A simple, limited-information Bayesian proxy-SVAR. For each posterior draw \((B_s, \Sigma_s)\) of a bvarm() fit, with residuals \(u_t^{(s)}\), the proxy is modelled by the measurement regression \(m_t = \Lambda' u_t + e_t\), \(e_t \sim N(0, \Sigma_e)\), with a flat (Jeffreys) prior on \((\Lambda, \Sigma_e)\). A draw of \((\Lambda_s, \Sigma_{e,s})\) from its (matrix-normal / inverse-Wishart) conditional posterior gives \(\mathrm{Cov}(u, m) = \Sigma_s\Lambda_s\) and \(\mathrm{Var}(m) = \Lambda_s'\Sigma_s\Lambda_s + \Sigma_{e,s}\), from which the impact vector is obtained exactly as in varm_proxy() (also for r > 1) and the responses are \(\Theta_h(B_s)\,\gamma_s\).

Usage

varm_proxy_bayes(
  fit,
  m,
  target = 1L,
  size = 1,
  horizon = 20L,
  level = c(0.68, 0.9),
  ndraw = NULL
)

Arguments

fit

a bvarm() object (class bvarm).

m

proxy: numeric vector, or T x r matrix of r proxies, aligned with the data (the first p rows are dropped to match the residuals).

target

variable(s) (name or position) whose impact response is normalised to size; length r.

size

size of the shock (impact response of target); scalar or length r.

horizon

maximum horizon (impact is 0).

level

confidence levels; bands are equal-tailed percentiles.

ndraw

number of posterior draws to use (default: all stored draws).

Value

a varm_proxy object with method = "bayes" (same layout as varm_proxy(), draws are posterior draws).

Details

Limitations (read before using). This is not the joint-likelihood Bayesian proxy-SVAR of Caldara & Herbst (2019) or Arias, Rubio-Ramirez & Waggoner (2021): the proxy does not enter the likelihood of the VAR, so it does not update \((B,\Sigma)\) and the reduced-form posterior is whatever the bvarm() prior implies; there is no prior on the structural parameters or on the instrument-shock relationship other than the flat prior on \(\Lambda\); stochastic-volatility fits (time-varying covariance) are rejected. With a weak instrument the posterior of the normalised responses is correctly wide (heavy-tailed) but, being Bayesian with a flat prior, its credible sets do not have frequentist coverage guarantees (use varm_proxy_robust() for those). Credible bands are equal-tailed posterior percentiles; estimate is the posterior median.

References

Caldara, D. and Herbst, E. (2019). Monetary policy, real activity, and credit spreads: evidence from Bayesian proxy SVARs. AEJ: Macroeconomics 11(1), 157-192.

Arias, J. E., Rubio-Ramirez, J. F. and Waggoner, D. F. (2021). Inference in Bayesian proxy-SVARs. Journal of Econometrics 225(1), 88-106.

Giacomini, R., Kitagawa, T. and Read, M. (2022). Robust Bayesian inference in proxy SVARs. Journal of Econometrics (doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2021.02.003); not implemented.

See also

varm_proxy(), varm_proxy_robust()

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
e <- matrix(rnorm(400), 200)
y <- matrix(0, 200, 2)
for (t in 2:200) y[t, ] <- 0.5 * y[t - 1, ] + c(e[t, 1] + 0.3 * e[t, 2], e[t, 2] + 0.5 * e[t, 1])
bf <- bvarm(y, p = 1)
varm_proxy_bayes(bf, m = e[, 1] + rnorm(200, sd = 0.5), horizon = 8, ndraw = 200)
#> <varm_proxy> shock to y1 (size 1), horizon 0..8, 200 posterior draws
# }
